reconcile.connective: Commentators read the Chronicles list as a compressed genealogy: the three are grandsons of Shem through Aram, with "sons" used loosely for descendants.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is catalogued by Steve Wells in the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, which lists Genesis 10:23 (sons of Aram) against 1 Chronicles 1:17 (sons of Shem) as giving two different fathers for Uz, Hul, and Gether.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Who was the father of Uz, Hul, and Gether?"
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (1999-), contradiction "Who was the father of Uz, Hul, and Gether?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/uz-hul-gether.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: The four following persons are called the sons of Shem, Ch1 1:17 being his grandsons, which is not unusual in Scripture …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Names both passages and resolves the tension directly: the Chronicles 'sons of Shem' are really Aram's sons, i.e. Shem's grandsons, a normal genealogical compression.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Meshech—or, "Mash"; these were the children of Aram, and grandsons of Shem (Gen 10:23).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Comments on the Chronicles verse itself and explicitly maps its names back to Aram as father and Shem as grandfather, citing Gen 10:23 — the harmonization at the point of tension.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Genesis 10:23
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this exact pair, noting the four are 'called the sons of Shem, Ch1 1:17 being his grandsons, which is not unusual in Scripture.' Used in place of Haley, whose specific coverage of this passage could not be confirmed.
